title: Reading: Vergil, Aeneid I.1–11
subtitle: Arma virumque canō. The opening of the Aeneid. First exposure to dactylic hexameter.
objectives: Read the opening lines of the Aeneid.
Understand epic diction and word order.

sections.heading: The opening of the Aeneid
sections.body:
Arma virumque canō, Troiae quī prīmus ab ōrīs
Ītaliam fātō profugus Lāvīniaque vēnit
lītora, multum ille et terrīs iactātus et altō
vī superum, saevae memorem Iūnōnis ob īram,
multa quoque et bellō passus, dum conderet urbem
īnferretque deōs Latiō, genus unde Latīnum
Albānīque patrēs atque altae moenia Rōmae.

(Gloss: arma — arms, war; vir — man; canō, -ere — to sing; Troia, -ae — Troy; quī — who; prīmus — first; ōra, -ae — shore, coast; fātum, -ī — fate; profugus — exiled, fugitive; Lāvinius — Lavinian; lītus, lītoris (n.) — shore; multum — much; ille — that (man); terra, -ae — land; iactō, -āre — to toss, drive; altum, -ī — the deep, sea; vīs, -is (f.) — force, violence; superī, -ōrum — the gods above; saevus — cruel; memor, -oris — mindful; Iūnō, -ōnis — Juno; ob — because of; īra, -ae — anger; passus (from patior) — having suffered; dum — until; condō, -ere — to found; īnferō, -ferre — to bring in; Latium, -iī — Latium; genus, generis (n.) — race, stock; unde — from which; Latīnus — Latin; Albānus — Alban; pater, patris — father (pl. senators, forefathers); altus — high; moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls.)

sections.heading: Translation guide
sections.body:
I sing of arms and the man, who first from the shores of Troy came exiled by fate to Italy and the Lavinian shores — much tossed on lands and sea by the force of the gods above, because of the mindful anger of cruel Juno, and having suffered much also in war, until he could found a city and bring his gods into Latium, from which (came) the Latin race and the Alban fathers and the walls of lofty Rome.

This is one sentence. Vergil delays the main verb ('canō') and immediately launches into a relative clause describing the man (Aeneas). Notice the compressed word order, the interwoven phrases, the alliteration (multum...memorem, altae...Albānī).

items.prompt: Who is the 'man' Vergil sings of?

items.answer: A city (Lavinium), from which came the Latin race and Rome.
